book.nourished.nourished_guide.compat_mo: Butchery is a meat processing mod that adds detailed cuts, organs, and exotic meats from nearly every mob in the game. Every Butchery item is fully classified as **Proteins** in Nourished, making it the single largest expansion to that food group in any supported mod.
Butchery

Butchery adds proper butcher cuts from vanilla animals — ribeye, sirloin, T-bone, rump steak, chuck steak, pork belly, pork loin, lamb loin, lamb rib, leg of lamb, chicken leg, chicken wing, ham, sausage, and more.

Each cut is a distinct protein family, meaning rotating through different cuts of the same animal still gives better nutrition than eating the same cut repeatedly.
Conventional Cuts
Detailed cuts, organs, and exotic meats for Proteins.

Butchery lets you process almost any mob — including hostile and boss mobs. These exotic meats are all classified as Proteins:

**Cooked Enderman Steak / Liver / Kidney** — hard to obtain but very high nutrition.
**Cooked Warden Meat** — extremely rare; treat as a luxury protein.
**Cooked Dragon Meat** — the ultimate exotic protein source.
**Cooked Creeper, Spider, Shulker** — common hostile mob proteins.
Exotic Meats
Butchery

Butchery adds organ meats including heart, liver, kidney, lungs, stomach, and intestines — all classified as Proteins.

Organ meats are distinct families from muscle cuts, so mixing organs into your protein rotation alongside steaks and chops gives excellent variety and keeps diminishing returns low.
Organs & Offal

With Butchery installed, the Proteins group has more variety than any other group. The risk is **defaulting to one favourite cut** and losing the benefit of all that variety.

Aim to rotate across at least three distinct families per day — for example a lamb cut, a fish fillet, and an organ meat. Use JEI and search **nourished:nutrients/proteins** to see the full list of what's available.
Rotation Strategy

Croptopia massively expands the crop roster and touches every food group. Its biggest impact is on **Fruits** and **Vegetables**, where it adds dozens of new families that make rotation trivially easy.

With Croptopia installed, maintaining a diverse diet becomes natural rather than deliberate.
Croptopia
A huge crop roster spanning every food group.

Croptopia adds many distinct fruit families. Key ones to grow:

**Strawberry** — fast-growing, excellent nutrition.
**Peach / Mango / Kiwi** — tree fruits, slower but high value.
**Grape** — vine crop; good density per plot.
**Pineapple** — tropical; high nutrition per harvest.
**Tomato** — fast, pairs well with vegetable rotation.
Fruits — Croptopia
Croptopia

Croptopia also adds to Proteins and Grains:

**Almonds / Peanuts / Cashews** — nut-family proteins; no animal farm needed.
**Tofu** — plant-based protein made from soybeans.
**Rice** — adds a Grains family distinct from wheat.
**Oats / Corn Flour** — alternative grain crops.

Nuts make a great supplemental protein for players who prefer less combat-heavy farming.
Proteins & Grains

With Croptopia, the main risk is **over-focusing** on a few favourite crops and ignoring the rest. The mod gives you so many options that it is easy to default to strawberries for Fruits every day.

Set up a multi-crop farm covering at least 3 distinct families per group. Croptopia's crop variety is only an advantage if you actually use it.
Rotation Advice

Croptopia vegetable additions include:

**Corn** — high-yield crop; excellent base vegetable.
**Onion / Leek** — fast-growing alliums; distinct family.
**Spinach / Lettuce** — leafy greens; quick crop cycle.
**Pepper / Chili** — spicy vegetables; unique family.
**Artichoke / Asparagus** — slow but high nutrition value.
Vegetables — Croptopia
How popular food mods integrate with Nourished and what they add to each food group.
A cozy farming overhaul focused on Vegetables and Grains.

Farm & Charm adds a cozy farming and cooking experience with new crops, animals, and processed foods. It integrates deeply with Nourished, expanding **Vegetables** and **Grains** the most, with smaller contributions to Fruits and Proteins.
Farm & Charm

The earliest Farm & Charm crops to plant for Nourished are **tomatoes** and **onions** — both fast-growing and immediately useful for expanding Vegetable rotation.

Once you have a cooking station, prioritize recipes that cover multiple groups. A single stew that covers Vegetables + Proteins is more inventory-efficient than carrying separate items for each group.
Getting Started

Farm & Charm adds new grain options:

**Oats** — a distinct grain family; can be used in porridge recipes.
**Rye Bread** — made from rye flour; higher nutrition than wheat bread.
**Cornbread** — requires corn; another distinct baked grain family.

These give Grains more rotation depth and make it easier to avoid diminishing returns on plain wheat bread.
Grains — Farm & Charm
Farm & Charm

Farm & Charm's cooking system produces multi-ingredient meals that often provide higher nutrition than their raw components and may count for **multiple food groups at once**.

A vegetable stew might cover Vegetables and Grains in one item. Check tooltips on cooked meals to see all groups they contribute to — meals are often more efficient than eating ingredients separately.
Processed Foods

Key Farm & Charm vegetables:

**Tomato** — fast-growing; distinct family from root vegetables.
**Onion** — quick crop; allium family.
**Pepper** — nightshade family alongside tomatoes.
**Pumpkin** (new variants) — expands the squash family.
**Leek / Radish** — root vegetables distinct from carrot and potato.
Vegetables — Farm & Charm

Farmer's Delight meals are where Nourished integration shines. Many dishes cover two or three groups in one item:

**Stew / Soup** — typically Vegetables + Grains.
**Roast Chicken** — Proteins + Vegetables.
**Bacon and Eggs** — Proteins + Dairy.
**Rice Bowl** — Grains + Vegetables.
**Stuffed Pumpkin** — Grains + Vegetables + Proteins.
Cooked Meals

The **Cooking Pot** is Farmer's Delight's crafting station for meals. Investing in one early pays off immediately for Nourished — cooking a pot of stew that covers three groups is far more inventory-efficient than carrying separate foods for each.

Prioritize recipes that cover your weakest groups. Check the tooltip of any cooked meal to see which Nourished groups it contributes to.
Cooking Pot
Multi-group meals that cover several bars in one item.

Farmer's Delight is a farming and cooking overhaul that adds crops, cooking tools, and a wide variety of prepared meals. Its biggest impact on Nourished is that many of its cooked dishes cover **multiple food groups at once**, making them incredibly efficient for maintaining all six bars.
Farmer's Delight
Farmer's Delight

Farmer's Delight adds several new crops that slot into existing groups:

**Tomato** — Vegetables; fast-growing and versatile.
**Onion** — Vegetables; distinct allium family.
**Rice** — Grains; introduces a new grain family separate from wheat.
**Cabbage** — Vegetables; leafy green family.
**Beetroot Seeds** (improved) — better yield than vanilla beetroot.
New Crops

Farmer's Delight meals each have their own food family, so rotating between different dishes avoids diminishing returns even when multiple dishes share a group.

A good daily rotation might be: **Roast Chicken** for lunch (Proteins + Veg), **Rice Bowl** for dinner (Grains + Veg), and a dairy item when needed. Three meals can cover every group with zero repetition.
Rotation Advice

Herbs & Harvest adds aged cheese varieties, each a distinct dairy family:

**Aged Swiss** — medium aging time; balanced nutrition.
**Aged Cheddar** — sharp flavour; high nutrition density.
**Aged Brie** — slow to produce but very high dairy value.

All three significantly outperform plain milk bucket in nutrition per item. Worth crafting once your dairy farm is established.
Dairy — Aged Cheeses
Artisanal cheeses, cured meats, and herb seasoning.

The earliest Herbs & Harvest addition to pursue for Nourished is the cheese process — milk a cow, follow the cheese aging recipe chain, and unlock the first multi-family dairy rotation.

Parallel to that, planting an herb garden gives seasoning options that improve almost every food group. A small herb plot is one of the best early investments when this mod is installed.
Getting Started

Herbs & Harvest focuses on artisanal food production — cured meats, aged cheeses, fermented products, and herb-seasoned dishes. Its biggest contribution to Nourished is **Dairy**, where it finally gives that group rotation options beyond plain milk.
Herbs & Harvest

The herb system in Herbs & Harvest can apply to many foods across groups. Seasoned variants of plain foods often have:

— Higher nutrition per item
— Slower diminishing returns (as a distinct family)
— Additional minor effects (saturation, speed)

Investing in herb farming pays off in higher food quality across multiple groups simultaneously.
Herbs & Seasoning
Herbs & Harvest

Herbs & Harvest adds cured and seasoned meats that count as Proteins:

**Cured Ham** — aged pork; high protein density.
**Smoked Salmon** — a distinct fish family separate from plain cooked salmon.
**Herb-Seasoned Beef** — cooked beef with herbs; improved nutrition over plain.

These give Proteins players more rotation variety and higher per-item nutrition.
Proteins — Cured Meats
How Nourished's effects step aside for LSO's own systems.

Legendary Survival Overhaul (LSO) is a survival mechanics overhaul that manages its own status effect system. Because LSO and Nourished would conflict when both try to apply effects simultaneously, [#](e05252)Nourished's bonus and penalty effects are disabled[#]() when LSO is installed.
Legendary Survival Overhaul
Legendary Survival Overhaul

The following are suppressed to avoid conflicts with LSO:

**Per-group bonuses** — e.g. Proteins max health, Grains XP gain.
**Per-group penalties** — e.g. Fruits health reduction, Dairy knockback.
**Balance Bonus** — the combined all-groups buff.

LSO handles survival effects through its own systems instead. Keeping your bars healthy still matters — it feeds into LSO's own calculations.
What Is Disabled

Even with effects disabled, the following Nourished systems work exactly as normal:

**All six nutrition bars** — track and decay as usual.
**Diet Screen** — fully functional.
**HUD overlay** — fully functional.
**Food tooltips** — freshness, family, group all shown.
**Diminishing returns** — still applies to nutrition gain.
**Sleep Bonus** — still applies if configured.
What Still Works

Even without Nourished's direct effects, your nutrition bars still feed data into LSO's survival systems. A well-balanced diet contributes positively to LSO's stamina, resilience, and recovery mechanics.

Think of Nourished as the **nutrition tracking layer** and LSO as the **effects layer** — they work together rather than duplicating each other.
Why Keep Bars Healthy?
Compat Mods

How Nourished detects and classifies foods from other mods.
Mod Compatibility

Nourished automatically detects installed food mods and assigns their foods to the appropriate groups via tag-based classification.

This chapter contains entries for supported mods. Entries only appear when the relevant mod is installed. If a mod you use is not listed here, its foods may still be classified automatically — check tooltips.
Mod Compatibility

Mods with dedicated book entries:

**Croptopia** — fruits, vegetables, nuts, grains.
**Farmer's Delight** — crops, multi-group cooked meals.
**Pam's HarvestCraft 2** — hundreds of crops across all groups.
**Legendary Survival Overhaul** — effects compatibility notes.
**Spice of Life: Onion** — how it interacts with diminishing returns.

Entries only appear when the relevant mod is installed.
Supported Mods
Hundreds of crops and recipes across every food group.

Pam's adds an enormous fruit roster — strawberries, raspberries, blueberries, blackberries, grapes, mangoes, papayas, figs, dates, and many more. Each is a distinct family.

With this many fruit options, the Fruits bar is one of the easiest to maintain. Grow a small orchard of 4–5 different fruit trees and you will never need to think about this group again.
Fruits — Pam's

With hundreds of options, the risk with Pam's is **analysis paralysis** — too many choices leading to no clear plan. Keep it simple:

Pick **one crop per group** to start with and build from there. A strawberry bush, a tomato plant, some oat seeds, and a cheese recipe covers four groups immediately and gives you a foundation to expand from.
Getting Started
**Grains:** Pam's adds oats, rye, corn flour, and a range of baked goods — muffins, pies, pancakes — each a distinct grain family.
Grains — Pam's
Pam's HarvestCraft 2

Pam's HarvestCraft 2 is one of the largest food content mods available, adding hundreds of crops, trees, and recipes across every food group. With Pam's installed, every Nourished group has so many options that diminishing returns become almost impossible to trigger.
Pam's HarvestCraft 2

Pam's expands animal products significantly:

**Proteins:** tofu, various nut-based proteins, additional fish varieties, and egg dishes provide plant-based alternatives to meat.
**Dairy:** butter, cheese, cream, and yoghurt give the Dairy group rotation options comparable to what Herbs & Harvest provides — multiple distinct families beyond plain milk.
Proteins & Dairy — Pam's

Pam's vegetable list is equally massive — corn, tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, zucchini, eggplant, leeks, scallions, and dozens more. Most are fast-growing row crops.

A Pam's vegetable garden covering 6–8 different crops will completely eliminate any risk of diminishing returns on Vegetables and keep the bar perpetually full.
Vegetables — Pam's

When your average nutrition is above 75%:

[#](52c252)+25% Stamina Regen[#]() — stamina recovers significantly faster.
[#](52c252)+10% Max Stamina[#]() — larger total stamina pool.
[#](52c252)-15% Stamina Usage[#]() — actions cost less stamina.
[#](52c252)+30% Penalty Decay[#]() — stamina exhaustion penalties fade faster.

All four bonuses are active simultaneously when the threshold is met.
Bonuses (avg > 75%)
How average nutrition drives stamina bonuses and penalties.

All six nutrition bars are averaged together into a single value. This average drives all stamina modifiers — it is **not** per-group. Keeping all six bars healthy is more important than maxing one or two.

[#](52c252)Above 75% average[#]() — bonuses apply.
[#](E8C24F)25% – 75% average[#]() — neutral, no modifier.
[#](e05252)Below 25% average[#]() — penalties apply.
How It's Calculated
Peak Stamina

Peak Stamina adds a stamina system for sprinting, jumping, and combat actions. When both mods are installed, Nourished modifies Peak Stamina's attributes in real time based on your **average nutrition level** across all six food groups.
Peak Stamina

When your average nutrition drops below 25%:

[#](e05252)-25% Stamina Regen[#]() — stamina recovers much slower.
[#](e05252)-15% Max Stamina[#]() — smaller total stamina pool.
[#](e05252)+25% Stamina Usage[#]() — actions cost more stamina.
[#](e05252)+30% Exhaustion Duration[#]() — stamina exhaustion lasts longer.

This combination makes low nutrition extremely punishing in combat and exploration.
Penalties (avg < 25%)

The 75% bonus threshold means keeping **all six bars above 75%** on average — not just one or two at full. A single bar at zero drags the average down significantly.

A player with five bars at 100% and one bar at zero has an average of ~83% — just above the bonus line. Let **two** bars hit zero and the average drops to ~67%, losing all bonuses. Keep every bar topped up.
Practical Advice
How two independent variety systems reinforce each other.

Nourished's diminishing returns and SoL's food history are separate counters. A food that is [#](e05252)saturated[#]() in Nourished (low nutrition multiplier) may still count as a [#](52c252)new entry[#]() in SoL's history if you have not eaten it recently.

This means you can strategically eat a wider range of foods to top up SoL's diversity counter while also rotating Nourished families — they reward the same behaviour.
Diminishing Returns & SoL

Both mods track food history, but they do so independently:

**Nourished** tracks variety at the item, family, and group level and applies it as a nutrition multiplier.
**Spice of Life** tracks a rolling history of unique foods eaten and grants rewards for diversity.

Eating a varied diet satisfies both systems at once — the same rotation that maximizes Nourished efficiency also earns SoL rewards.
How They Interact
Spice of Life: Onion

With both mods installed, the optimal strategy is simply to eat as many **different foods** as possible each day rather than defaulting to a small rotation.

Instead of eating bread + apple + steak every day, try rotating through 10–15 different foods across the week. Both mods reward this heavily — Nourished via freshness bonuses and SoL via its diversity rewards.
Practical Advice

Spice of Life: Onion is a food variety mod that independently tracks food history and rewards eating a diverse diet. It works alongside Nourished rather than replacing it — both systems run simultaneously and reinforce the same core goal: **eat variety, not repetition**.
Spice of Life: Onion

The Dairy bonus — increased armor toughness — makes incoming damage more predictable and reduces the effectiveness of high-damage hits.

This makes Dairy especially valuable in combat-heavy playthroughs. Players who fight frequently or play on hard difficulty should treat this group as a high priority.
Armor Toughness Bonus
Bone-strengthening foods that increase armor toughness.

Two cows is the minimum for a sustainable dairy setup — one to breed from, one to milk. Three or more ensures you always have milk available without waiting.

Keep your cow pen close to your base. Dairy is the easiest group to maintain once you have any cows at all — the challenge is remembering to actually bucket them each day.
Farming Tips

Herbs & Harvest adds aged cheeses including Swiss, cheddar, and brie. These provide significantly higher dairy nutrition than plain milk and introduce distinct cheese families for rotation. See the **Compat Mods** chapter for more.
Dairy — Herbs & Harvest

The Dairy penalty — reduced knockback resistance — means depleted Dairy makes you easier to push around in combat. This is especially dangerous around ledges, lava, or enemies that spam attacks.

Keep this group above zero before entering any dungeon or boss fight.
Knockback Resistance Penalty
Dairy

Dairy foods strengthen bones and body. [#](e05252)Penalty:[#]() reduced knockback resistance when depleted. [#](52c252)Bonus:[#]() increased armor toughness when maintained. A single cow pen keeps this group topped up easily.
Dairy

Milk bucket is your only vanilla dairy source. Since there is no rotation possible, diminishing returns do not apply the same way — just bucket a cow every morning and evening and this group stays healthy with minimal effort.
Dairy — Vanilla

**Milk Bucket** — the primary vanilla dairy source. Bucket a cow whenever passing by.

Vanilla has only one dairy item, which means this group has almost no rotation options without a food mod installed. The upside: there is nothing to overthink. Keep a cow, bucket regularly.
Vanilla Dairy Sources
Explore each food group, their bonuses, and the foods that belong to them.

With Croptopia installed, the Fruits group expands significantly. Strawberries, peaches, mangoes, kiwis, and many more exotic fruits are available. See the **Compat Mods** chapter for the full Croptopia food list.
Fruits — Croptopia
Sweet, vitamin-rich foods that speed up regeneration.

Melon farms are among the most space-efficient for Fruits. A 3×3 patch of melon stems produces enough slices to keep this group topped up indefinitely.

Sweet berry bushes planted in rows are low-maintenance. They grow without irrigation and produce reliably each season without replanting.

**Golden Apple** and **Enchanted Golden Apple** both count as Fruits and give high nutrition — but they are expensive luxuries, not reliable staples.

Save them for emergencies. A melon farm is far more cost-effective for keeping this group stable day to day.
Golden & Enchanted
Fruits

Fruits has several distinct food families: Apple, Berry, and Melon. Rotating across all three gives you better nutrition gain than eating only apples.

If you have Croptopia or another fruit mod installed, you have even more families to rotate through — check tooltips to see which family each fruit belongs to.
Rotation Strategy

Fruits are sweet, vitamin-rich foods. [#](e05252)Penalty:[#]() reduced max health when depleted. [#](52c252)Bonus:[#]() increased regeneration speed when maintained. Apples, melons, and berries all count.
Fruits

Sweet berries are one of your most accessible wild fruit sources alongside apples and melons. Keep a berry bush farm early on to maintain this group easily.

Apple trees near your base make passive top-ups effortless — just grab drops when you pass by.
Fruits — Vanilla

**Apple** — drops from oak and dark oak trees. Plant a small orchard early.
**Sweet Berries** — found wild in taiga biomes; bushes are renewable and fast.
**Melon Slice** — grown from seeds found in dungeon chests or jungle temples.
**Glow Berries** — found in lush caves; low nutrition but accessible early.
Vanilla Fruit Sources

Pumpkin pie and other baked goods also count toward Grains. They provide higher nutrition values than plain bread, making them worth crafting once you can supply the ingredients reliably.

Keep a pumpkin farm and you always have access to pie as a high-value grain top-up.

Staple foods that speed up experience gain.

The Grains bonus — faster experience gain — is one of the most impactful in the game for combat and enchanting progression.

Prioritizing Grains early is especially worthwhile if you plan to enchant gear or grind XP. The bonus stacks with other XP sources and applies passively while it is active.
Experience Bonus

Wheat is the most fundamental farm crop and the backbone of the Grains group. A moderate wheat farm covers this group indefinitely with bread alone.

Automating a bread farm — harvest wheat, craft bread, store — is one of the easiest and most impactful nutrition automations you can build early in a world.
Farming Tips
Grains

Bread, cookie, and pumpkin pie are all distinct grain families. Rotating between them gives better nutrition than eating only bread each day.

Cake is a special case — each slice of the same cake is the same item, so eating an entire cake counts as eating the same food repeatedly. Pair cake slices with other grain foods on the same day for best efficiency.
Rotation Strategy

Grains are staple foods that form the backbone of any diet. [#](e05252)Penalty:[#]() reduced hunger restoration when depleted. [#](52c252)Bonus:[#]() faster experience gain when maintained. Bread is your most reliable source.
Grains

**Bread** — crafted from 3 wheat; the most cost-efficient grain per crop.
**Cookie** — 8 cookies per craft; high volume, lower nutrition per piece.
**Cake** — placed block; each slice gives grain nutrition. Good for group eating.
**Pumpkin Pie** — excellent nutrition value; worth the pumpkin investment.
Vanilla Grain Sources
Food Groups
Rich, sustaining foods that increase max health.

A cow, pig, and chicken pen near your base covers three distinct protein families at once. Breed them regularly — you want a surplus, not just enough to survive.

If you are playing early-game without a farm, keep a fishing rod ready. Fishing covers Proteins reliably with no infrastructure required and also produces bonus loot.

**Cooked Salmon** and **Cooked Cod** are excellent early-game proteins available near any river or ocean before you have an animal farm established.

Fishing also yields **Tropical Fish** which counts as Proteins, though it has low nutrition. Use it as a supplement rather than a primary source.
Fish Sources

Cooked salmon and cod are excellent protein sources and easy to obtain near any river or ocean. A fishing rod from early game makes this group trivial to maintain before any farm is built.

Auto-fishing farms are very effective for this group if you want a fully passive protein supply.

Proteins

Not all proteins come from animals. Several plant-based and processed foods also count:

**Cooked Chicken Egg** (if enabled) — high nutrition density.
**Mushroom Stew** — counts as Proteins in many configurations.

Check tooltips on any food item to confirm which group it belongs to on your server.
Non-Meat Proteins

Each animal type is its own protein family. Eating beef, then porkchop, then chicken gives better returns than eating three steaks in a row.

Fish counts as a separate family from land meat — switching between a cooked salmon and cooked beef at the same meal is an easy way to avoid diminishing returns on both.
Rotation Strategy

Proteins are rich, sustaining foods. [#](e05252)Penalty:[#]() reduced attack damage when depleted. [#](52c252)Bonus:[#]() increased max health when maintained. Cooked meats and fish are your primary sources.
Proteins

**Cooked Beef** — highest nutrition of vanilla meats; keep a cow farm.
**Cooked Porkchop** — nearly equal to beef; pigs breed quickly.
**Cooked Chicken** — lower nutrition but very common and fast to farm.
**Cooked Mutton** — solid mid-tier protein from sheep.

Hearty, grounding foods that improve hunger saturation.

Farm & Charm adds tomatoes, onions, peppers, and more. These introduce new vegetable families and significantly expand rotation options. See the **Compat Mods** chapter for the full Farm & Charm food list.

Carrots and potatoes are the most efficient vanilla vegetables to farm — they replant themselves and grow quickly with irrigation.

A mixed row of carrots, potatoes, and beetroot covers three distinct vegetable families. Plant them side by side in alternating rows to make rotating your diet effortless.

**Golden Carrot** is the single highest-nutrition vanilla vegetable. It fills the bar noticeably more than a plain carrot and also provides excellent hunger saturation.

If you have a gold surplus, a small stock of golden carrots makes a great emergency top-up for the Vegetables group.
Golden Carrot
Vegetables

The main vanilla vegetable families are Carrot, Potato, and Beetroot. Rotating through all three maximizes your nutrition gain compared to eating only one type.

Noting that **baked potato** and **raw potato** share a family — cooking improves nutrition value but does not count as variety. Use both baked and raw in a pinch, but branch out to carrots and beetroot for best results.
Rotation Strategy

Vegetables are hearty, grounding foods. [#](e05252)Penalty:[#]() reduced movement speed when depleted. [#](52c252)Bonus:[#]() improved hunger saturation when maintained. Carrots, potatoes, and beetroot all qualify.
Vegetables

Beetroot is your best secondary vegetable alongside carrots and potatoes. A small mixed crop farm covers this group reliably from early game onward.

Vegetables — Vanilla

**Carrot** — found in village farms or zombie drops; very easy to obtain early.
**Potato** — also found in villages; bake for higher nutrition value.

Vanilla Vegetable Sources
book.nourished.nourished_guide.food_safe: What happens when you eat raw food, and how your gut handles the damage.

Beyond gut health, keeping specific nutrient bars topped up builds direct **resistance** to raw food penalties — reducing how hard each event hits before it even happens. Different tiers respond to different groups:

[#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() resistance comes from [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]() and [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]().
[#](E85D75)Medium[#]() resistance comes from [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]().
[#](E85D75)Severe[#]() resistance comes from [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]().
Building Resistance
The hidden stat that makes repeated raw eating worse over time.

Your gut flora is a separate hidden stat that tracks how well your digestive system is holding up.

It starts healthy and decays when you eat raw food. Let it get low enough and it starts amplifying the penalties you take — a bad gut makes raw food even worse.
Gut Health

Every raw food event damages your gut flora by an amount based on the tier. [#](E85D75)Severe[#]() foods do the most damage, [#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() foods do the least.

Gut damage doesn't happen instantly from one bad meal — it accumulates. Eating raw occasionally is survivable. Making it a habit is not.
How It Decays

Gut flora recovers two ways. Eating **cooked** food gives an immediate boost proportional to how well-cooked it is — a fully cooked meal helps more than a barely-seared one.

It also regenerates passively over time, and that passive rate gets a **diversity bonus** the more balanced your overall diet is. A well-rounded diet across all six groups isn't just good for your bars — it heals your gut faster too.
How It Recovers
Gut Health

Cook your food whenever possible. Keep your overall diet balanced to speed up gut recovery, and pay attention to Proteins in particular — it contributes to resistance against both Medium and Severe raw food.

If your gut is already low, prioritize cooked meals until it recovers before worrying about the rest of your bars.
The Takeaway
Food Safety
What happens when you skip the campfire.

Eating raw meat and other uncooked foods [#](E85D75)isn't free[#](). Nourished tracks what you eat and penalizes you when you skip the campfire.

The penalty scales with how raw the food is — there are three tiers: **Mild**, **Medium**, and **Severe**. Foods that are fine raw (bread, apples, carrots) skip all of this entirely.
Eating Raw Food

Nourished remembers recent raw food events for a short window. If you eat the same raw item again inside that window, the system does not roll a fresh random debuff — it **extends the one you already have**, stacking its duration on top.

Back-to-back raw meals of the same item make the debuff last longer, not shorter. Switching to a cooked meal (or a different food entirely) breaks the chain.
Eating the Same Food Again

[#](E85D75)Medium[#]() penalties apply to clearly raw foods — standard raw meats like beef, pork, and chicken.

The nutrient penalty is larger and a significant portion of the nutrition is lost compared to eating the cooked version. You are also more likely to trigger gut flora damage at this tier.
Medium

[#](E6C65C)Mild[#]() penalties apply to foods that are technically edible raw but clearly not ideal — lightly processed or borderline items.

You take a small nutrient penalty and miss out on a portion of the nutrition the cooked version would have given. Not a disaster, but it adds up.
Mild

Every tier includes a **missed opportunity** multiplier. This is the fraction of nutrition the cooked version would have given that you simply don't get.

Eating raw doesn't just hurt you — it wastes the food. A raw beef gives far less Protein than a cooked one, even before the penalty kicks in.
Missed Opportunity
Raw Food

[#](E85D75)Severe[#]() penalties apply to foods that should never be eaten raw under any circumstances.

Nutrient bars take a meaningful hit, nearly all of the cooked nutrition is denied, and your gut flora takes the hardest damage. Just cook it.
Severe

Each food group shows a **fill bar** representing your current level. Bars drain over time through nutrient decay.

Hover over a bar to see the exact value, your active bonus or penalty, and which foods you have recently eaten in that group.

When all of the food groups are above their threshold, you gain the [#](F5A623)**Balance Bonus**[#](), a persistent buff that improves health, speed, or other stats depending on your configuration.

Keeping the bonus active should be your primary goal.
Bonuses and penalties tied to each food group.

Letting any group fall to zero applies a [#](E85D75)**penalty**[#]() for that group. Penalties stack: neglecting multiple groups at once causes increasingly severe debuffs.

Recovery is straightforward: eat foods from the depleted group and the penalty fades as the bar refills.

Each food group has its own bonus active when healthy:

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#](): [#](FFB84D) increased regeneration speed.[#]()

[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#](): [#](8FE388) improved hunger saturation.[#]()

[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#](): [#](F0808F) increased max health.[#]()

[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#](): [#](F2D77C) faster experience gain.[#]()

[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#](): [#](8CCCF0) increased armor toughness.[#]()

[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#](): [#](4F9E4F) reduced movement speed.[#]()

A survival guide for your first day with Nourished active.

See the How It Works chapter for the full details.

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#](): Berry bushes, apple-bearing trees, and melon patches.

Sleep when all five bars are above their threshold and wake up with the [#](B88CFF)**Sleep Bonus**[#](). This is the ideal daily rhythm Nourished is designed around.

[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#](): Bread from village chests, or seeds to plant wheat immediately.

Once you are past day one, check out the Tips & Tricks chapter for deeper strategies:

[#](F5A623)**Daily Routine**[#](): the ideal loop for keeping all bars healthy.

A small mixed farm is the most reliable long-term strategy. Plant [#](E6C65C)**wheat**[#](), [#](7BC96F)**carrots**[#](), [#](7BC96F)**potatoes**[#](), and [#](7BC96F)**beetroot**[#]() early.

Keep a cow pen nearby for milk and cooked beef. Even a tiny farm can cover most of your core food groups with minimal effort.

When you first spawn, all the nutrition bars start at a moderate level. You won't feel any effects immediately, but they will begin to decay.

Your priority on day one is to gather a variety of foods before the bars run dry.
Reading a food's group and nutrition value at a glance.
The tooltip shows the food's **group**, its **nutrition value**, and its **family**. Foods from the same family give diminishing returns — variety within a group matters as much as the group itself.
Hover over any food item to see which food group it belongs to and how much nutrition it provides.

Press [#](F5A623)**H**[#]() to enter [#](B88CFF)**Edit Mode**[#](). In edit mode you can drag the HUD to any position on your screen.

Press [#](F5A623)**H**[#]() again to lock it back in place. Your [#](7BC96F)**position**[#]() is saved between sessions.

The HUD can be positioned wherever it is most convenient for you while playing.

The [#](8CCCF0)**Nutrition HUD**[#]() displays your current nutrition levels at a glance.

Each bar represents one of your food groups, making it easy to see which parts of your diet need attention without opening a screen.

[#](F5A623)**The Core Idea**[#]()

There are five food groups:

[#](F5A623)**Fruits**[#]()
[#](7BC96F)**Vegetables**[#]()
[#](E85D75)**Proteins**[#]()
[#](E6C65C)**Grains**[#]()
[#](6FB8E8)**Dairy**[#]()

Maintaining each group provides [#](6FB8E8)**bonuses**[#](), while neglecting them causes [#](E85D75)**penalties**[#](). [#](F2D77C)**Balance**[#]() is everything.
What Nourished is and how it changes the way you eat.

[#](B88CFF)**Welcome to Nourished**[#]()

Nourished adds a nutrition system that encourages eating a [#](B88CFF)**varied diet**[#](). Each food group you consume contributes to your overall [#](7BC96F)**health**[#]() and [#](F5A623)**performance**[#]().

Eat well, sleep soundly, and your body will reward you.

When a food group drops [#](E85D75)**critically low**[#](), Nourished sends a [#](F5A623)**toast notification**[#]() in the top-right corner of your screen.

Toasts appear once per group when they cross the critical threshold. Pay attention to them, or your stats will suffer.
Toast warnings and food-eaten calorie notifications.

Every time you eat, Nourished also shows a small [#](F5A623)**food eaten**[#]() notification with the item's name and how many [#](7BC96F)**calories**[#]() it added.

Eating the same food again quickly merges into the same notification instead of stacking a new one each bite — it just updates in place.
Nourished uses [#](F5A623)**notifications**[#]() to warn you when your nutrition needs attention.

You can disable [#](B88CFF)**notifications**[#]() in the mod's config if you prefer to manage nutrition manually.

The [#](6FB8E8)**HUD mini bars**[#]() will still change color as groups reach critical levels, giving you a passive visual warning at all times.
The reward for going to bed well-nourished.

Filling [#](7BC96F)**all Five groups**[#]() to a [#](7BC96F)**healthy level**[#]() before bed gives the [#](F2D77C)**maximum bonus**[#]() — a burst of [#](E85D75)**regeneration**[#]() and a small boost to your [#](6FB8E8)**nutrient levels**[#]() on waking.

Neglecting your diet means waking up feeling no better than when you went to sleep.
A well-balanced diet makes for better rest. When you sleep, your nutrition determines the strength of your [#](B88CFF)**Sleep Bonus**[#]() when you wake.
book.nourished.nourished_guide.how_it_wo:
The [#](B88CFF)Balance Score[#]() measures how evenly spread your nutrition is across all six groups — not how full any single bar is.

It compares each bar to the average of all of them. Five groups full and one empty scores worse than all six sitting at a moderate, even level. It's shown on the left panel of the diet screen.
Balance Score
How evenly spread your nutrition is, not how full any one bar is.

The score isn't a fixed pass/fail band — it's continuous. The further any bar drifts from the average of the rest, the more the score drops, whether that bar is unusually low or unusually high.

[#](7BC96F)Even[#]() coverage across all six groups keeps the score high. [#](E85D75)Lopsided[#]() eating — maxing one or two bars while others sit empty — drags it down even if your total nutrition looks fine on paper.
Even vs. Uneven
Balance Score
A deeper look at the systems behind Nourished.

The food tooltip shows your current freshness for any item:

[#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() — full or bonus nutrition, novelty active.
[#](E6C65C)Reduced[#]() — diminishing returns pulling the multiplier down.
[#](E85D75)Saturated[#]() — heavily repeated, near the floor.

Check this before eating if you're trying to efficiently top up a specific bar.
Checking Your Status
Why the fifth apple of the day barely moves the bar.

Eating the same food repeatedly gives [#](E85D75)less nutrition each time[#](). The first apple of the day fills your Fruits bar noticeably. The fifth apple barely moves it.

This system exists to reward variety over repetition.
Diminishing Returns

Diminishing returns aren't tied to sleeping or the in-game day — they fade continuously based on real time elapsed since you last ate that food.

Give something a break for a while and its multiplier recovers on its own. There's no need to wait for morning; just eat something else in the meantime.
How It Fades
Diminishing Returns

Eating something you haven't touched in a while gives a [#](7BC96F)novelty bonus[#]() that pushes the multiplier above 1.0 — genuinely diverse eating gives more nutrition than the safe, familiar choice.

The tooltip shows [#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() when the novelty bonus is active on a food.
The Novelty Bonus

Nourished tracks how much you've recently leaned on a food at three levels simultaneously: the **specific item**, its **family**, and its **food group**.

These aren't three separate penalties stacked on top of each other — they blend into one multiplier. Early on, the item-specific level dominates. The more you've recently eaten broadly from that family or group, the more those broader levels start pulling your multiplier down too.
Three Levels at Once
The middle layer between a single food and its whole group.

Within each food group, foods are organized into **families**. All apple-type foods, for example, share the Apple family.

Family is the middle of the three levels Diminishing Returns tracks — between the specific item and the whole food group. Lean on one family for a while and it starts dragging down everything in that family, not just the one item.
Food Families
Food Families

You can check a food's family in its tooltip. Ideally you want to rotate across **multiple families** within each group, not just multiple foods.

Eating an apple, then a golden apple, then an enchanted golden apple is still all Apple family — real variety means switching to melons or berries instead.
Why It Matters

Your **Balance Score** doesn't multiply nutrition directly — instead, a well-balanced diet speeds up passive Gut Health recovery, and Gut Health itself amplifies every raw-food penalty you take when it's low. See the previous entry and the Food Safety chapter for both.
Balance and Gut Health
How every bonus and penalty in this chapter fits together.
Multiplier System

None of these systems need to be memorized in detail. The practical takeaway is consistent across all of them: cook your food, rotate what you eat across items and families, and spread your meals across groups instead of running one at a time.

Do that, and most of this chapter simply never comes up.
Putting It Together

Everything in this chapter feeds into one question: how much nutrition does this specific meal actually give you? Two things can push that number up:

[#](7BC96F)Cooking:[#]() eating something cooked avoids the raw food penalty entirely — see the Food Safety chapter.
[#](7BC96F)Novelty:[#]() eating a food you haven't touched in a while gives a one-time boost on top of its normal value.
The Bonuses

And several things can push it down:

[#](E85D75)Diminishing Returns:[#]() repeating the same item, family, or group recently reduces its multiplier.
[#](E85D75)Streak:[#]() eating the exact same item again soon makes that drop steeper.
[#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt:[#]() overeating one group past a threshold drains whichever group you've neglected most.
The Penalties
How It Works

The fix is the same as everything else in this chapter: rotate. Spreading your meals across groups instead of running one group at a time keeps your eat-count on any single group below the threshold, so debt never triggers in the first place.

A high Balance Score and staying out of Nutritional Debt go hand in hand — both reward the same even, varied diet.
Avoiding It
The cost of leaning on one food group for too long.
Nutritional Debt

[#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt[#]() isn't about letting a bar sit empty — it's the cost of eating too narrowly. Lean hard on one food group over and over, past a configurable threshold, and the system starts looking for payback.
Nutritional Debt

Once that threshold is crossed, Nourished finds whichever group you've been [#](6FB8E8)neglecting[#]() the most — your lowest bar, excluding the one you're currently overeating — and drains it a little.

In other words: bingeing on Proteins doesn't just fail to help your other bars, it can actively cost you whichever one you've been ignoring.
Who Pays for It

Eating any **different food** breaks the streak immediately. You don't need to switch groups — just switch items.

The streak counter shows in the food tooltip when it's active, so you always know before you take the hit.
Breaking the Streak
Why the third bread in a row hits harder than the first.
Streak Penalty

Eating the same food back-to-back applies a [#](E85D75)Streak Penalty[#](). Three meals of plain bread in a row? The third gives noticeably less grain nutrition than the first.

A streak isn't a separate system bolted onto Diminishing Returns — it's what makes that item's diminishing-returns count climb faster than normal. Eating it again soon after adds a bigger hit to the same counter instead of a normal-sized one.
Streak Penalty

book.nourished.nourished_guide.server_ow:
Nourished exposes every bonus and penalty as a status effect entry in a config file. Server owners can change which potion effect is applied, its amplifier and duration, and the nutrient threshold that triggers it — no restart required.

The config lives at [#](B88CFF)config/nourished/effects.json[#]().
Configuring Effects
Tuning the potion effects tied to each nutrient bar.

To turn off a specific bonus or penalty, set its [#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() field to [#](6FB8E8)false[#](). The nutrient bar keeps tracking as normal — the entry is simply skipped when deciding which effects to apply.

This is useful for lighter server experiences or modpacks with their own progression systems. Built-in effects are only regenerated into the file if it is missing or invalid, so a disabled entry stays disabled.
Disabling Effects

Each entry in the array is one effect tied to one nutrient:

[#](6FB8E8)effect[#]() — the status effect id to apply, e.g. [#](6FB8E8)minecraft:weakness[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)nutrient[#]() — the nutrient key this entry watches, or [#](6FB8E8)all[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)trigger[#]() — [#](6FB8E8)below[#](), [#](6FB8E8)above[#](), or [#](6FB8E8)all_above[#](): when the effect fires relative to [#](6FB8E8)threshold[#]().
[#](6FB8E8)amplifier[#]() / [#](6FB8E8)duration_ticks[#]() — potion strength and how long it lasts.
[#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() — set [#](6FB8E8)false[#]() to disable the entry without deleting it.
Effect Entry Fields
Configuring Effects

After editing [#](B88CFF)effects.json[#](), run [#](6FB8E8)/nourished reload[#]() to pick up the change without restarting the server.

Effects registered by other mods through the API or KubeJS are merged into this same file at runtime, so it always reflects everything currently active.
Reloading Changes
Configuration options and per-item overrides for server administrators.
Correcting or reassigning how a specific item is classified.

Nourished supports per-item [#](B88CFF)value overrides[#]() for nutrients and calories. This lets server owners and modpack makers correct or reassign how any specific item is classified without touching the mod itself.

Overrides live at [#](B88CFF)config/nourished/food_overrides.json[#]().
Food Value Overrides

Run [#](7BC96F)/marieslib dump nourished_nutrients[#]() (or the "Export All Foods" button in the Scanner tab of the config screen) to write a reference folder — one file per nutrient, listing every item Nourished currently resolves into that category with its live values.

These export files are read-only reference; editing them does nothing by itself.
Getting Starting Values

An override entry has [#](6FB8E8)item[#](), [#](6FB8E8)nutrients[#](), [#](6FB8E8)calories[#](), and [#](6FB8E8)enabled[#]() fields. It is merged over normal classification, not a full replacement:

Any nutrient key you list wins outright — including a value of [#](6FB8E8)0[#](), which zeroes that nutrient out entirely.
Any key you omit still falls back to whatever Nourished would normally classify for that item.
[#](6FB8E8)calories[#]() is always a full override when present.
How Overrides Merge
Food Value Overrides
After editing [#](B88CFF)food_overrides.json[#](), run [#](6FB8E8)/nourished reload[#]() to pick up the change without restarting the server.

You do not need to eat from all five groups at every meal. Instead, eat 2–3 groups per sitting and rotate which groups you cover each time.

Example rotation:
**Morning:** [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]() + [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]()
**Midday:** [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() + [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]()
**Evening:** [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]()

This keeps all bars healthy without ever feeling like a chore.
Batch Eating

Before entering a dungeon, raid, or boss fight, check that these two groups are above their good threshold:

[#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() — bonus max health helps survive burst damage.
[#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() — bonus armor toughness reduces effective incoming damage.

If either is low, eat a cooked steak and bucket a cow before you go in. The difference in survivability is significant.
Before a Fight

Planning to enchant gear or grind a mob farm? Make sure your [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() group is well above the bonus threshold before you start.

The Grains bonus — faster experience gain — passively increases all XP earned while active. A pumpkin pie and a loaf of bread before your session can meaningfully speed up an enchanting or leveling run.
Before an XP Session
A simple daily rhythm that keeps every bar healthy.

Glance at the HUD bar overlay regularly — not just when you feel effects. Bars drop slowly and you want to catch them before they hit the critical threshold, not after.

If a bar is in the [#](E85D75)red range[#](), address it immediately. If it is in the [#](E6C65C)yellow range[#](), eat something from that group before your next sleep.
The HUD is Your Friend

Nourished is designed around a simple daily rhythm. Follow this loop and you will rarely suffer a penalty:

**Morning:** eat one food from any low group before leaving base.
**During the day:** eat normally for hunger; rotate food types.
**Evening:** top up any bars below 50% before sleeping.
**Sleep:** with all bars healthy to earn the Sleep Bonus.
The Ideal Daily Loop
Daily Routine
Practical strategies for staying balanced, recovering quickly, and getting the most out of Nourished.

If you can only keep one or two animal pens early on, choose:

**Cows** — cover both Dairy (milk) and Proteins (cooked beef). The single most efficient animal for Nourished.
**Bees** — passive honey supply with zero daily effort once hives are set up. Useful for recipes even without a separate sweets group.

Chickens are lower priority since their protein value is lower, but they breed quickly and are easy to maintain.
Animal Priority

A few simple automations make Nourished almost invisible:

**Auto-wheat harvester** — keeps bread in constant supply.
**Dispenser + water harvester** — hands-off carrot and potato farming.
**Auto honey collector** — dispensers with bottles harvest hives automatically when full.
**Auto fish farm** — provides passive protein with no mobs required.
Automation Ideas
A small, well-planned farm covers every food group.

If you can only tend a few crops, prioritize these:

**Wheat** — most versatile; makes bread, cake, and cookies.
**Pumpkin** — makes pumpkin pie (high-value Grains).
**Melon** — the easiest renewable Fruit at scale.
**Carrots** — fast-growing, no replanting needed, renewable golden carrots.
High-Value Crops

You do not need a mega-farm to stay healthy. A surprisingly small setup covers all five groups:

**Wheat patch** — covers [#](E6C65C)Grains[#]() via bread.
**Carrot + potato rows** — covers [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]().
**Melon or berry patch** — covers [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]().
**Cow pen (2+)** — covers [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]().
**Chicken or pig pen** — covers [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]().
The Minimal Farm
Efficient Farming

Keep a dedicated **nutrition chest** near your base — a small chest stocked with one stack each of your six key foods.

Refill it during farm harvests and draw from it when a bar is low. This prevents emergency scrambles and means you always have something from each group on hand when you need it.
Storing Supplies
How to recover quickly when multiple bars hit critical.
Emergency Recovery

If a bar has been at zero for a sustained period, you may be in [#](E85D75)Nutritional Debt[#]() — a stronger debuff state. Refilling the bar does not immediately clear debt.

To recover: keep the group above zero consistently. Do not let it drop back to empty while recovering. Eat from that group multiple times over the next in-game day to work off the debt.
Nutritional Debt

Keep these high-nutrition emergency foods in your inventory for quick recovery:

**Cooked Beef** — fastest [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() top-up per item.
**Golden Carrot** — fast [#](7BC96F)Vegetables[#]() recovery.
**Apple** — widely available, decent [#](F5A623)Fruits[#]() nutrition.
**Milk Bucket** — instant [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() coverage and also removes debuffs.
Quick Fix Foods

Sleep is the most powerful recovery tool in Nourished. Even if not all bars are above the bonus threshold, sleeping with all bars above **zero** prevents debt accumulation and gives a partial recovery.

If you are in a rough state, prioritize getting every bar above the critical line, then sleep. The next morning you will be in a much better position to top up properly.
Sleep to Recover

**Milk Bucket** not only fills the Dairy bar — it also removes all active status effects including nutrition penalties.

If you are stacking multiple penalties at once, drinking a milk bucket gives you a clean slate and buys time to properly address the underlying bar levels. Keep at least one in your hotbar when venturing far from home.
The Milk Trick

If multiple bars hit critical at once — maybe after a long trip far from base — do not panic. Address groups one at a time, starting with the penalty that hurts most in your current situation.

[#](E85D75)In combat or exploring:[#]() fix Proteins (attack) and Dairy (knockback) first.
[#](7BC96F)Back at base:[#]() fix Fruits (health regen) and Vegetables (saturation) for recovery.
When Things Go Wrong
Staying nourished on the road and with a crew.

For long dungeon or nether runs where you cannot eat freely between fights, prioritize **pre-loading** your bars before entering:

— All six groups above 60%
— [#](E85D75)Proteins[#]() and [#](6FB8E8)Dairy[#]() at or above bonus threshold
— Milk bucket in hotbar for emergency debuff clear

Bars decay slowly enough that a two-hour session rarely causes a problem if you start fully topped up.
Long Dungeon Runs
Multiplayer & Adventure

In multiplayer, a shared farm benefits everyone. Consider assigning different players to maintain different groups:

**Farmer** — wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot.
**Rancher** — cows, pigs, chickens, bees.
**Forager** — collects wild fruits, mushrooms, fishing.

A well-organized community farm makes Nourished invisible for the whole server.
Shared Farms

Village trading is an underrated nutrition tool. Farmer villagers often sell:

**Bread** — cheap Grains in bulk.
**Apple** — easy early Fruits.
**Cooked Chicken** — decent Proteins trade.
**Pumpkin Pie** — excellent value Grains.

Early-game trading can cover multiple nutrition groups before your own farm is established.
Trading for Nutrition

When leaving base for extended exploration, pack food from all six groups — not just your usual hunger food. A nutrition emergency two thousand blocks from home is much worse than one in your base.

A good travel kit: cooked beef, carrot, apple, bread, honey bottle, and a milk bucket. That covers all six groups in six inventory slots.
Traveling Far from Base
Tips & Tricks
Reading a food's group, nutrition, and freshness at a glance.

Hover over any food item to see Nourished tooltip information below the item name:

**Food Group** — which bar this food fills.
**Nutrition Value** — how much it fills the bar under ideal conditions.
**Food Family** — which family it belongs to for diminishing returns.
**Freshness** — whether this food currently gives full, reduced, or bonus nutrition.
Food Tooltips

The [#](7BC96F)freshness indicator[#]() tells you how much nutrition you will actually receive:

[#](7BC96F)Fresh[#]() — first time eating this food today; full or bonus nutrition.
[#](E6C65C)Reduced[#]() — diminishing returns active; lower nutrition than base.
[#](E85D75)Saturated[#]() — heavily repeated; minimal nutrition gain.

If a food shows Saturated, switch to a different family within that group for better returns.
Freshness Indicator

If you have JEI installed, you can filter the entire item list by food group. Type any of these into the JEI search bar:

**nourished:nutrients/fruits**
**nourished:nutrients/vegetables**
**nourished:nutrients/proteins**
**nourished:nutrients/grains**
**nourished:nutrients/dairy**
JEI Tag Search

This is the fastest way to answer the question **"what can I eat right now?"** when a bar is low.

JEI will show every item on the server assigned to that group — including modded foods — so you can see at a glance what you have in your inventory or nearby chests that qualifies.
JEI Tag Search (cont.)
Reading Tooltips

When the streak penalty is active, the tooltip shows a [#](E85D75)streak counter[#](). This appears after eating the same food consecutively without switching.

If you see this, eat one different food before continuing with your usual diet. Even a single item from a different food family resets the streak and restores full multipliers.
Streak Warning

If a food item shows **Unclassified** or no Nourished tooltip at all, it has not been assigned to a food group on this server.

For modded foods this is usually resolved by the server's datapack configuration. If you believe a food should belong to a specific group, contact your server admin or check the Nourished datapack documentation in the **Server Owners** chapter.
Unrecognized Foods
